images.caption: View of the entrance area of the Treasury of the Basilica of Saint Servatius in Maastricht, Netherlands. This photo was taken during the Heiligdomsvaart pilgrimage, a seven-yearly religious and cultural festival that dates back to the Middle Ages. It meant that many objects had been removed from the Treasury to be shown in the church on Saturday 2 June, or to be included in the procession on Sunday 3 June. The empty showcase in the centre for instance usually contains the silver-gilded reliquary bust of Saint Servatius.
images.alt: View of the entrance area of the Treasury of the Basilica of Saint Servatius in Maastricht, Netherlands. This photo was taken during the Heiligdomsvaart pilgrimage, a seven-yearly religious and cultural festival that dates back to the Middle Ages. It meant that many objects had been removed from the Treasury to be shown in the church on Saturday 2 June, or to be included in the procession on Sunday 3 June. The empty showcase in the centre for instance usually contains the silver-gilded reliquary bust of Saint Servatius.

images.caption: Maastricht, the Netherlands. View towards the East of Plein 1992, the main square of the Céramique neighbourhood on the East bank of the river Meuse, named after the Treaty of Maastricht (1992). The square was designed in the late 1990s by Dutch architect Jo Coenen, as well as several buildings around it, including the Centre Céramique library on the right. To the left: part of La Résidence by Swiss architect Aurelio Galfetti and French architect Yann Keromnes. At the far end: a fragment of La Fortezza by Mario Botta.
